claims.text: The target material is a quaternary equiatomic FCC alloy.
The target microstructure contains coherent phase interfaces and a hierarchical pattern similar to HPHT-treated Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer between phases, alleviate stress concentration, and enable synergistic deformation.
A hierarchically patterned microstructure promotes strain delocalization through the activation of multiple deformation mechanisms.
At low strain rates, deformation is controlled by thermally activated dislocation climb or glide over obstacles.
Increasing strain rate makes the thermal activation barrier for dislocation glide less significant relative to applied stress.
The rate-limiting mechanism shifts from thermally activated glide to athermal dislocation transmission across coherent interfaces as strain rate increases.
When interface crossing becomes the dominant bottleneck, further increases in strain rate do not significantly increase yield stress.
Yield strength will plateau between 10^-3 and 10^-1 s^-1 at room temperature.
Conventional FCC alloys dominated by thermally activated glide show a logarithmic or monotonic increase in yield strength with strain rate.
Thermally activated dislocation motion in the proposed baseline alloys has a stress exponent of approximately 3–5.
Incoherent interfaces cause strain localization, incompatible deformation, interfacial cracking, or premature failure in untreated Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
The proposed strain-rate plateau requires coherent interfaces and a hierarchically patterned microstructure.
At sufficiently high strain rates, inertial effects, twinning, or phase transformation can supersede interface-controlled dislocation transfer.
Deformation twins and microbands can interact with dislocations and contribute to strain hardening at large plastic strain.
The plateau range depends on constituent-specific activation energies and the nature of the coherent interfaces.
Phase stability is sensitive to pressure or stress state.
A continuous logarithmic yield-strength increase with m greater than 0.01 would indicate that thermally activated glide remains rate-limiting.
Dominant twinning or phase transformation at the intermediate strain rate would falsify interface-controlled dislocation transfer as the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The target is described as quaternary and equiatomic, but the stated analogue Al0.7CoCrFeNi contains five elements and is non-equiatomic.

The material is presented as an FCC alloy, while the proposed mediator includes FCC/B2 interfaces and deformation in multiple phases; this implies a multiphase FCC+B2 material rather than an unqualified single-phase FCC structure.
